articles.title: Generating AutoCAD R12 (AC1009) ASCII .DXF Files in Pure TypeScript: 8 AIA Layers, $INSUNITS Inches, and Screen-to-CAD Arc Math
articles.excerpt: If you have ever exported a floor plan from a consumer browser tool only to open it in AutoCAD, BricsCAD, QCAD, or LibreCAD and see every wall, door swing, cabinet, and dimension flattened onto Layer…
articles.body: If you have ever exported a floor plan from a consumer browser tool only to open it in AutoCAD, BricsCAD, QCAD, or LibreCAD and see every wall, door swing, cabinet, and dimension flattened onto Layer 0 at arbitrary pixel coordinates, you know why contractors and drafters reject SVG-to-DXF converters. Real drafting software expects true 1:1 US inch coordinates, clean right-handed Cartesian geometry, separated AIA-style layers with distinct AutoCAD Color Index (ACI) colors, and valid DXF header and table records that never trigger a file-recovery prompt. When we built the zero-dependency CAD export engine inside PlanCaliber , we targeted AutoCAD R12 ( AC1009 ) ASCII .DXF directly from pure TypeScript.

articles.title: Designing a Loyalty Rewards Program for Offline Brands: An Event Driven Approach
articles.excerpt: Most loyalty software is built for ecommerce, where you already know the customer, the order and the basket. Offline brands have a harder problem. A tube of adhesive or a pack of tea passes through a…
articles.body: Most loyalty software is built for ecommerce, where you already know the customer, the order and the basket. Offline brands have a harder problem. A tube of adhesive or a pack of tea passes through a distributor, a wholesaler and a corner shop before anyone buys it, and the brand never learns who that buyer was. This post walks through how to design a loyalty rewards program for that world, using product level QR codes as the entry point and events as the backbone. The core idea Every unit carries a unique code. A scan is the moment an anonymous buyer becomes a known customer. Everything else in the program reacts to that one event.

articles.title: Fake Uniswap Google Ads Stole $400K+. The Protocol Was Never Hacked.
articles.excerpt: Search "Uniswap" on Google and the first result might take everything. That is not a hypothetical. It happened in May 2026. Attackers bought Google sponsored advertisements for the "Uniswap" keyword,…
articles.body: Search "Uniswap" on Google and the first result might take everything. That is not a hypothetical. It happened in May 2026. Attackers bought Google sponsored advertisements for the "Uniswap" keyword, pointed them at a phishing site that looked identical to the real exchange, and drained anyone who connected a wallet and signed a transaction. Total losses: more than $400,000. Two attacker wallets collectively held about 146 ETH, roughly $306,000 at the time of the report. Uniswap's smart contracts were never compromised. There was no reentrancy bug, no oracle manipulation, no flash loan, no clever math error. The vulnerability was not in the protocol. It was in the entry point. The attack, step by step Attackers purchased sponsored ads for the keyword "Uniswap" on Google Search.

articles.body: How many addresses has Circle blacklisted on USDC? As of 28 November 2026, Circle's native USDC contracts on six EVM chains have blacklisted 957 distinct addresses , and 750 of them are still blacklisted. On Ethereum alone the count is 915 addresses ever and 716 now. The pace has jumped: 2026 has 2,011 blacklistings across these chains so far, against 782 in all of 2025. The addresses still blacklisted hold 1,041,938,804.86 USDC that cannot move while they stay blacklisted, and 85.2% of it sits at addresses blacklisted on a single day: 29 October 2026, when news reports said Circle froze about $823 million in USDC after the Binance hack. Figures quoted in the press range from 372 to 596 addresses.

articles.title: How Scan to Win Assured Cashback Works Under the Hood: Single Use QR Codes at Scale
articles.excerpt: Product QR cashback is everywhere in India now: scratch the hidden panel on a pack, scan, and money lands in your wallet. It looks simple from the outside. Under the hood, a scan to win assured cashba…
articles.body: Product QR cashback is everywhere in India now: scratch the hidden panel on a pack, scan, and money lands in your wallet. It looks simple from the outside. Under the hood, a scan to win assured cashback campaign is a small security system that has to stop reuse, guessing, and counterfeit packs, while still responding in under a second. Here is how a system like Assured Rewards approaches the problem, and what any developer building something similar should think about. 1. Code generation: make guessing pointless Each pack gets a unique code. If codes are sequential, someone will script through them. So: Generate codes from a cryptographically secure random source, not Math.random() . Use enough entropy. A 12 character base32 code gives about 60 bits, which makes brute force impractical.

articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.
